newsitem.title: INDIA: India to ship tea to Iraq under oil for food plan.
newsitem.headline: India to ship tea to Iraq under oil for food plan.

text.p: India's Tea Board said on Friday it had secured permission to export 1,000 tonnes of black tea to Iraq under the U.N.-supervised "oil-for-food" programme.

A statement from the Tea Board said India's Tata Tea had secured an order to ship 1,000 tonnes of tea "which the company is expected to export in the immediate future. The approval was received by both the Tea Board and Tata Tea today."
The statement did not specify how much Iraqi crude oil India would receive as part of the tea export deal.
Asked how much crude was involved, a Tea Board official said: "I cannot tell you that. I am not allowed to speak other than on the clearance of exports of tea to Iraq."
Petroleum Ministry officials declined to say how much crude India would receive.
A senior Petroleum Ministry official said the new oil-for-food package with Iraq had yet to be completed since Iraq was still negotiating with the United Nations for relaxation of some conditions.
In the oil-for-food plan that ended in May this year, India contracted three cargoes of crude oil amounting to 50,000 tonnes at an average of $19 per barrel, he said.

Iraq is expected to more than double its oil exports next month to around 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) to make up for a gap between the end of the first "oil-for-food" deal and the beginning of the second.

The second deal began on June 8 but Iraq has delayed exporting oil for two months and will now have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than previously reckoned, or forego some of its oil sales under the scheme.
The United Nations confirmed late on Wednesday that Iraq must sell around $1.0 billion worth of oil by early September under the renewed oil-for-food deal.
The Indian Tea Board official, who did not wish to be identified, said permission had been granted by the U.N. Iraq sanctions committee.
The contract was signed by Tata Tea and Iraq's Food Stuff Trading Company, the Tea Board statement added.
Tata Tea is among the largest tea makers in the world. Its exports in 1996/97 (April-March) jumped 106 percent to 2.16 billion rupees ($60.6 million).

"In a remarkable breakthrough, India has secured permission to export a thousand tonnes of black tea to Iraq, tea trade with which country virtually came to a standstill since the (1990) war," the Tea Board statement said.
It said India's shipments of tea to Iraq had peaked "in the mid-eighties with about 13,000 tonnes".
